requirements.statement: The child MUST NOT execute its target unless applying the profile, confirming the sandbox and consuming its tokens all succeeded; spawning MUST return an error naming the failed step and OS error; spawning MUST be refused when the apply-method probe has not shown a caged child with a denied canary.

acceptance.given: a cage and a child whose apply step is made to fail
acceptance.then: it returns an error naming the step and the target never runs

acceptance.given: the first spawn of the process
acceptance.then: it reports the apply method usable only after a throwaway child is caged and its canary access is denied

acceptance.given: a policy granting one directory
acceptance.then: the kernel refuses with EPERM

tasks.text: [US1] [SR-001] Implement `src/macos/probe.rs`: `probe()` runs once per process. It compiles `(version 1)(deny default)`, spawns `/usr/bin/true` with a pre_exec that applies, verifies and requires `open("/private/etc/hosts")` to fail with EPERM, then returns the `PROBE_OK` marker. The result is `ApplyMethod::PathA`, or a cached `Unsupported::ApplyMethod`.
[US1] [SR-001] [SR-004] Write the base-policy helper and US1 tests in `tests/spawn_macos.rs` (`#![cfg(target_os = "macos")]`):

requirements.statement: Spawning from an already-sandboxed process MUST return AlreadySandboxed without forking a target.

acceptance.given: a process that is itself a caged child
acceptance.then: it gets AlreadySandboxed and no grandchild runs

requirements.statement: Private libsandbox symbols MUST be resolved at runtime before any fork, and a missing symbol MUST yield Unsupported naming it; unsafe code MUST be confined to macos::sys with a SAFETY comment on every block.

acceptance.given: a symbol name that does not exist
acceptance.then: it returns Unsupported naming the symbol and OS build

acceptance.given: the root crate
acceptance.then: unsafe code outside macos::sys fails the build and every unsafe block has a SAFETY comment

tasks.text: [SR-003] Update the root `Cargo.toml`: version `0.0.2`; `[dependencies] procage-policy = { path = "crates/procage-policy", version = "0.0.1" }`; `[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies] libc = "0.2"`; replace `[lints] workspace = true` with the workspace set but `unsafe_code = "deny"`. Update `crates/procage-policy/Cargo.toml` to version `0.0.1`, publishable, with a description of the companion crate. Run `cargo deny`.

[P] [SR-003] Write `tests/unsafe_confined.rs`: scan `src/` for the token `unsafe`. It is allowed only in `src/macos/sys.rs`, and there each occurrence must have `// SAFETY:` within the 3 lines above it.

requirements.statement: Between fork and exec the child MUST only issue system calls on parent-prepared data; at least 100 caged children spawned from a parent with four threads under dyld contention MUST all be caged with none hanging.

acceptance.given: four threads looping dlopen/dlsym/dlclose
acceptance.then: all deny their canary access and none exceeds a 10 s timeout

tasks.text: [US1] [SR-001] [SR-004] Write the base-policy helper and US1 tests in `tests/spawn_macos.rs` (`#![cfg(target_os = "macos")]`):

requirements.statement: Every policy path MUST be resolved to its real, firmlink-visible spelling before lowering (longest existing prefix, remainder byte-exact, glob prefix escaped), with each rewrite recorded.

acceptance.given: a policy granting write to /tmp/<dir>
acceptance.then: it succeeds and the cage records the rewrite to /private/tmp/<dir>
acceptance.when: the child creates a file via /tmp

acceptance.given: a path not yet existing below /tmp
acceptance.then: the existing prefix is resolved and the remainder kept

acceptance.given: a glob under /tmp whose resolved prefix contains a glob character
acceptance.then: the character is escaped and matched literally

tasks.text: [P] [US2] [SR-005] Implement `src/macos/canon.rs`: `resolve(&AbsPath)` (longest existing prefix, remainder byte-exact, `/System/Volumes/Data` mapped to the visible form when dev and inode match); glob prefix resolution with escaping; `resolve_policy(&Policy) -> Result<(Policy, Vec<PathRewrite>), SpawnError>` covering fs targets, unix sockets and raw Seatbelt filters.

requirements.statement: A grant token MUST be issued per spawn, of class procage.<name>, for a resolved existing path, and MUST unlock only that grant for that spawn; undeclared grant names and missing paths MUST be typed errors; an unbound grant MUST give no access.

acceptance.given: one cage with a write grant, bound to A then to B
acceptance.then: each succeeds only in its own directory
acceptance.when: two children write to A and B

acceptance.given: an unbound grant
acceptance.then: access is refused

acceptance.given: a binding for an undeclared name or a missing path
acceptance.then: it fails with a typed grant error

tasks.text: [US3] [SR-006] Implement grant binding in `src/macos/spawn.rs`: undeclared name → `GrantError::Undeclared`; resolve, and a missing path → `Missing`; `issue_file("procage.<name>")`, and null → `Issue`; tokens moved into the closure.

requirements.statement: Compiled profiles MUST be cached only in memory, keyed by the exact profile text and parameters.

acceptance.given: the same policy prepared twice
acceptance.then: no compile happens

acceptance.given: two policies differing in one rule
acceptance.then: two compiles happen

requirements.statement: A profile over the in-process compile limit MUST be refused with LimitExceeded before libsandbox is called.

acceptance.given: a policy over the configured limit
acceptance.then: it fails with LimitExceeded and the compile counter is unchanged

requirements.statement: The child's environment MUST be exactly the policy's allowlist (or passthrough minus denied names) of the caller's environment plus variables set explicitly on the command.

acceptance.given: the caller has SECRET_TOKEN and PATH set and the policy allowlists PATH
acceptance.then: it shows PATH and not SECRET_TOKEN

acceptance.given: passthrough denying SECRET_TOKEN
acceptance.then: SECRET_TOKEN is absent and other variables are present

requirements.statement: With Tty::None the child MUST start a new session without a controlling terminal; Tty::NewPty MUST be refused with Unsupported until implemented.

acceptance.given: Tty::None
acceptance.then: it leads its own session and has no controlling terminal
acceptance.when: the child queries its session and opens /dev/tty

acceptance.given: Tty::NewPty
acceptance.then: it fails with Unsupported naming the setting

requirements.statement: Crate docs and the threat-model release status MUST state what this development version enforces on macOS (each claim backed by a caged-child test) and what it does not (fd hygiene, descendant lifetime, base profile, Linux); escape-class statuses MUST stay unchanged until escape-suite canaries exist.

acceptance.given: the crate docs, README and threat model
acceptance.then: every enforcement sentence maps to a test in tests/spawn_macos.rs and the inherited-fd gap is stated
